items.title: Person dead in Toronto police-involved shooting in Mississauga
items.summary: One person is dead following a police-involved shooting in Mississauga. m. on Thursday, Peel Regional Police. Toronto Police were conducting an investigation in the area, and reports indicate shots were fired after a collision. Peel police said one male was left with life-threatening injuries, and the Special Investigations Unit had invoked its mandate. In an update, the SIU said the incident was now fatal. One other male was transported to hospital with minor injuries, police said. A Toronto Police officer was also transported to hospital with minor injuries as a result of a collision, police said. Three people were taken into custody, police said.

items.title: Mississauga shooting leaves man with life threatening injuries, SIU investigating
items.summary: One person has died and others are injured following an officer-involved shooting. Ontario’s police watchdog says it’s investigating a fatal police shooting in Mississauga on Thursday morning. m. when the incident occurred, according to an X post by Peel police. The Special Investigations Unit (SIU), confirmed there was a fatality in a post to X. According Peel police, one man has life threatening injuries and another was taken to hospital with minor injuries. Peel police did not answer The Star’s questions about how the men were injured. A Toronto police officer was also transported to hospital with minor injuries due to a collision. However the SIU nor Peel Police confirmed if the person who died was one of the injured. Three people are in custody and there are no outstanding suspects. Police have not provided any suspect descriptions.

items.title: 1 critically injured, 3 arrested in Mississauga police shooting
items.summary: A male victim is dead, and three people are under arrest after an officer‑involved shooting in Mississauga overnight, prompting a response from Toronto police, Peel police and Ontario’s police watchdog. m. on Thursday conducting an investigation when the shooting occurred. One male suffered life‑threatening injuries and was rushed to a hospital, where he later died, the province’s police watchdog confirmed with CityNews. Three people were taken into custody at the scene. A second male was also transported to hospital with minor injuries. Investigators say no suspects are outstanding, and the situation is contained. A Toronto police officer was taken to the hospital with minor injuries after a collision connected to the incident. No details have been released about how the crash occurred or whether it was related to the shooting. A Toronto police spokesperson wouldn’t elaborate on specifics, only saying that officers were in the area as part of an investigation. Peel police say a heavy police presence remains in place and the neighbourhood will stay closed for several hours. The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) has invoked its mandate, which is required whenever police are involved in an incident resulting in serious injury, death, or allegations of sexual assault.

items.title: Shots fired in Mississauga as Toronto police investigation leaves suspect fighting for life
items.summary: A man is in hospital with life-threatening injuries after an officer-involved shooting during a Toronto police investigation in Mississauga early Thursday. In an update, the Special Investigations Unit said one person had died. m. According to Peel Regional Police, Toronto Police Service officers were conducting an investigation when shots were fired. One man suffered life-threatening injuries and was transported to hospital. Three people were taken into custody and police say there are no outstanding suspects. A Toronto police officer was also taken to hospital with minor injuries after being involved in a collision related to the incident. Another man was transported to hospital with minor injuries. The Special Investigations Unit has invoked its mandate and will investigate the circumstances surrounding the police shooting. Peel police say a heavy police presence remains in the area and roads around Council Ring Road and The Collegeway are expected to remain closed for several hours while investigators examine the scene.

items.title: US$73-million contract makes Mississauga NBA star one of city’s richest athletes
items.summary: Dillon Brooks has never shied away from playing the villain on the basketball court. Now, the Mississauga native has another title to add to his résumé: one of the richest professional athletes ever to come out of the city. The 30-year-old Phoenix Suns forward has agreed to a three-year, US$73-million contract extension that will keep him with the team through the 2029-30 NBA season. The fully guaranteed deal comes after the best offensive season of Brooks’ career and will push his total career earnings to more than US$200 million by the time the contract expires. That places Brooks among the highest-paid athletes ever produced by Mississauga, alongside fellow NBA star RJ Barrett, who signed a five-year, US$120-million contract extension with the New York Knicks in 2022. com photo) Born and raised in Mississauga, Brooks developed into one of Canada’s top basketball prospects before attending Father Henry Carr Catholic Secondary School in Toronto and later starring at the University of Oregon. He led the Ducks to the NCAA Final Four in 2017 and was named Pac-12 Player of the Year before being selected 45th overall in the NBA Draft. Although drafted by the Houston Rockets, Brooks was traded to the Memphis Grizzlies on draft night, where he quickly established himself as one of the league’s toughest perimeter defenders. He spent six seasons in Memphis, earning NBA All-Defensive Second Team honours in 2023 while helping define the Grizzlies’ physical style of play. His reputation only grew after signing a four-year, US$86-million contract with the Houston Rockets in 2023. Two seasons later, he was dealt to Phoenix as part of the blockbuster trade that sent Kevin Durant to Houston.

items.title: Matty Matheson's Maker Pizza Picks a 31-Storey City Centre Condo for Its Next Location
items.summary: According to INsauga, Maker Pizza, the fast-growing Toronto pizza chain co-founded by celebrity chef Matty Matheson, is set to open its second suburban location inside Mississauga's Exchange Signature Residences, a 31-storey condo tower near Square One. The chain's first suburban outpost opened in Thornhill, and INsauga reports the Mississauga location will sit inside the Exchange District, a new residential development in the City Centre neighbourhood. A countdown on Maker Pizza's website points to an opening in just over three weeks, following an announcement the company made earlier this summer. The exact menu for the Mississauga location hasn't been released yet, but INsauga notes the chain is known for slices like the truffle shuffle, a bechamel-based pie called Frank's Best, and a chili-pineapple Tropic Thunder pizza, alongside a classic cheese pie. Beyond pizza, the restaurant also serves chicken wings and garlic fingers. For Mississauga's City Centre, the opening adds another dining option to a neighbourhood already anchored by Square One and its growing cluster of condo towers.

items.summary: Police in Waterloo region have arrested and charged a Mississauga man in the death of a Cambridge man last month. Police say the Cambridge man took part in a private ibogaine healing experience. Ibogaine is a psychoactive alkaloid that is not authorized for use in Canada.

items.title: A 200-Year-Old Streetsville Log Cabin Traces Back to the Family Behind Toronto's Leslieville
items.summary: According to INsauga, Toronto's Leslieville neighbourhood takes its name from George Leslie, one of the sons of a family that once lived in what is now Mississauga's Leslie Log House. The book Leslieville, written by Joanne Doucette and published in 2016, documents how the Leslie family sailed from Scotland to Canada in 1825, landing in Quebec in mid-May, before John Leslie travelled ahead alone to a property in what was then Toronto Township. INsauga reports John Leslie, his wife Esther Beattie Leslie, and their children later built and lived in the log house on land the family leased, and eventually purchased, from King's College, keeping the property in the family for a century. The home was originally built just north of Derry Road in Meadowvale before being relocated in 1994 to its current site at 4415 Mississauga Rd. in Streetsville. Built in 1826, the log house is one of the oldest surviving log homes in Ontario and holds designated heritage status, with the city marking its 200th anniversary this past weekend. The connection means a piece of east Toronto's identity traces directly back to a family whose original homestead still stands in present-day Mississauga.

items.title: Loose Screens and Balcony Furniture Are Bigger Fall Risks Than Most Residents Realize, City Warns
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, falls from windows and balconies can cause serious injury or death, though the city says many of these incidents are preventable through simple precautions under its Balcony Basics awareness campaign. The city identifies common hazards as furniture placed too close to windows or balcony railings, windows left unsecured, and screens that were never designed to stop a fall in the first place. Young children face the highest risk, while older adults can be more vulnerable because of mobility or balance issues, the city says. Renters and highrise residents are encouraged to learn how to recognize these hazards themselves and report concerns early rather than waiting for something to go wrong. The responsibility doesn't stop with tenants. The city says property owners, landlords and building managers must also keep safety features in working order and respond quickly once a problem is flagged. Mississauga backs up the campaign with education, inspections and enforcement action aimed at preventing injuries before they happen.
